video_title: Believing Brown Trade Explanation? + Where Will Brad Stevens & Celtics Go From Here?

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Celtics' decision to trade Jaylen Brown was driven by relationship deterioration
quotes.excerpt: the relationship with Jaylen Brown reached a point of no return

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: They stuck to their script, which was basically that they don't know if this trade is going to work for them or not. They were trying to be very respectful to Jaylen Brown. They were saying, 'We're not sure, we felt like we had to do this.' And he kept saying for optionality. I don't think they were 100% saying why they did it. They made it sound like this was a real tough call, they were on the fence. I'm sure it was a tough call. He said he lost sleep over what the reaction would be. I think they feel confident in their decision.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: They were full of crap when they acted like the relationship with Jaylen Brown didn't deteriorate and wasn't a factor in this decision. It was a driving force in the decision. You can't tell me both that money didn't matter and it wasn't about any of that stuff. Now, I believe the money part because you didn't really save money right away on this deal. And by the way, this deal ultimately is going to be judged by what are you able to flip Paul George's expiring contract next year plus a bunch of picks into.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Paul George's trade kicker impact on Celtics' salary cap
quotes.excerpt: Paul George waived his trade kicker, which would have been I think like 3.9 million
quotes.quote: He got asked directly, how can you talk about money because Paul George and Jaylen Brown make about the same amount of money. Although Bobby Marks reported yesterday that Paul George waived his trade kicker, which would have been I think like 3.9 million. The Sixers would have had to pay that, the actual write the check, but it would have hit the Celtics' books. It would have cut their space under the apron to less, and it would have been split over the two years. It's only 2 million dollars, but it would have split there. It's interesting that Paul George waived his trade kicker. I don't think Paul is probably upset that it's out there because it kind of is an indication to the Celtics, 'I'm happy to be here.'

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Celtics' trade exception and potential roster moves
quotes.excerpt: Boston has two things to watch now. Number one, they have the Anthony Simons trade exception
quotes.quote: Boston has two things to watch now. Number one, they have the Anthony Simons trade exception, which I think is around 27 million dollars. They have these extra picks. They could use that trade exception to acquire a player with their picks or somebody else's picks. They don't have to use it now. It doesn't expire till mid-season, a year from the deal. I'm not even sure where they're going to end up under the aprons. They may not even do that. Because they used the full mid-level on Mitchell Robinson, their hard cap at the first apron. So I'm not saying they're going to go out there and trade for a star player in the next 10 minutes, but just know that that exists.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Peyton Pritchard's extension eligibility and role
quotes.excerpt: Peyton Pritchard is extension eligible. And he is on an extremely attractive contract
quotes.quote: The second thing to keep an eye on is that Peyton Pritchard is extension eligible. And he is on an extremely attractive contract, 7.5 this year, 8 million dollars, 8.5 next year. He is 29 years old. I don't think you're necessarily want to give him a four-year extension unless it's really good money. But whether or not they extend Peyton, I expect them, part of this, I think is they're going to boost even boost Peyton Pritchard's role even more and build out more for him. And so it probably makes, if you think that you're going to build an even bigger role for Peyton Pritchard, it makes sense to sign him now before he maybe has even a bigger season than he did a year ago.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Bucks' trade demands were higher than reported
quotes.excerpt: the what the Bucks wanted was more than what has been reported
quotes.quote: From what I understand, the what the Bucks wanted was more than what has been reported. It wasn't just Hugo Gonzalez and Giannis Antetokounmpo. I think they were asking for more draft capital and maybe more other players.
